assays.assay_description: Mice were placed in an open field with an overhead camera immediately after i.p. psilocybin (5 mg/kg) or saline; head twitches were manually scored from video over the first 15 min by a blinded experimenter, in Emx1-Cre+ and littermate control mice of both sexes.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin ... was injected intraperitoneally (i.p.) at a dose of 5 mg/kg

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were placed in an open field with a camera positioned directly above for 30 min immediately after drug administration

food_restriction.evidence: Standard open field arena; no food described in the apparatus during recording

water_restriction.evidence: Standard open field arena; no water described in the apparatus during recording

time_to_assay.evidence: Mice were placed in an open field ... immediately after drug administration to record head twitch responding

sample_size.evidence: N = 20 mice (10 males, 10 females; 10 Emx1-Cre-, 10 Emx1-Cre+) were used to assess the acute behavioral effects of psilocybin.

outcomes.summary: A single 5 mg/kg dose of psilocybin robustly increased head twitch counts over the first 15 min post-injection in both Emx1-Cre+ (forebrain excitatory 5-HT1BR knockout) and littermate control mice, with no effect of genotype or sex.
outcomes.statistics: main effect of psilocybin: F(1, 16) = 131.50, p < 0.0001; main effect of genotype: F(1, 16) = 0.93, p = 0.93; main effect of sex: F(1, 16) = 0.31, p = 0.584
outcomes.evidence: Mice treated with psilocybin demonstrated significantly more head twitches than mice treated with saline over the 15 min following injection (Fig. 2A; main effect of psilocybin: F(1, 16) = 131.50, p < 0.0001).

assays.assay_description: Locomotor activity recorded in the open field for the full 30 min immediately after i.p. psilocybin (5 mg/kg) or saline and analysed with EthoVision; time course over 30 min and area under the curve reported, in Emx1-Cre+ and control mice of both sexes.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin ... was injected intraperitoneally (i.p.) at a dose of 5 mg/kg

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were placed in an open field with a camera positioned directly above for 30 min

food_restriction.evidence: Standard open field arena; no food described in the apparatus during recording

water_restriction.evidence: Standard open field arena; no water described in the apparatus during recording

time_to_assay.evidence: Mice were placed in an open field ... for 30 min immediately after drug administration

sample_size.evidence: N = 20 mice (10 males, 10 females; 10 Emx1-Cre-, 10 Emx1-Cre+) were used to assess the acute behavioral effects of psilocybin.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (5 mg/kg) significantly reduced locomotor activity over the 30 min post-injection in both genotypes, confirmed by AUC analysis; there was no genotype difference, and a marginal drug x sex interaction.
outcomes.statistics: main effect of psilocybin: F(1, 16) = 8.66, p = 0.0095; drug x genotype interaction: F(1, 16) = 0.86, p = 0.368; AUC main effect of psilocybin: F(1, 16) = 9.43, p = 0.007; AUC drug x genotype: F(1,16) = 0.70, p = 0.414; drug x sex: F(1,12) = 5.16, p = 0.042; drug x genotype x sex: F(1,12) = 0.043, p = 0.839
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin significantly reduced locomotor activity in both controls and Emx1-Cre+ mice (Fig. 2B, main effect of psilocybin: F(1, 16) = 8.66, p = 0.0095).

B1_num_measures.evidence: Locomotion was analyzed using EthoVision software for the full 30 min; the AUC is a summary of the same locomotor variable

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Locomotor activity is shown for both Emx1-Cre- and Emx1-Cre+ mice over 30 min following drug administration (Fig. 2B); Area under the curve for locomotion was calculated using the trapz function

assays.assay_description: Mice were placed in the centre of an elevated plus maze (arms 35 x 5 cm, 60 cm above floor, ~200 lx) facing a closed arm and videotaped for 5 min, 48 h after psilocybin or saline; open arm entries and time in open arms were scored with EthoVision in Emx1-Cre+ and control mice of both sexes.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin ... was injected intraperitoneally (i.p.) at a dose of 5 mg/kg

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice were placed in the center of the maze facing a closed arm and videotaped while freely exploring the maze undisturbed for 5 min

food_restriction.evidence: No food present in the elevated plus maze during the 5-min test

water_restriction.evidence: No water present in the elevated plus maze during the 5-min test

time_to_assay.evidence: Mice were tested for anxiety-like behavior in the elevated plus maze (EPM) 48 h after drug administration.

sample_size.evidence: N = 58 mice (28 males, 30 females; 24 Emx1-Cre-; 34 Emx1-Cre+) were used to assess post-acute anxiety-related behavioral effects of psilocybin.

outcomes.summary: 48 h after a single dose, psilocybin increased open-arm entries and time spent in open arms in Emx1-Cre- control mice, indicating anxiolysis; these effects were attenuated in Emx1-Cre+ mice lacking forebrain excitatory 5-HT1BRs. No sex effect was detected.
outcomes.statistics: Open arm entries: drug x genotype interaction F(1, 52) = 4.14, p = 0.046; controls mean difference = -3.87, 95% CI [-7.71, -0.05], p_adj = 0.046; Emx1-Cre+ mean difference = -0.04, 95% CI [-3.27, 3.19], p_adj = 0.998; drug x genotype x sex F(1, 48) = 0.008, p = 0.930. Time in open arms: main effect of psilocybin F(1, 49) = 7.36, p = 0.009; drug x genotype F(1, 39) = 1.94, p = 0.170; controls mean difference = 6.61, 95% CI [0.37, 12.85], p_adj = 0.034; Emx1-Cre+ mean difference = 2.33, 95% CI [-2.96, 7.61], p_adj = 0.647; drug x sex F(1, 45) = 3.512, p = 0.067
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin significantly increased the number of open arms entries in Emx1-Cre- controls (mean difference = -3.87, 95% CI [-7.71, -0.05], p_adj = 0.046), but not in Emx1-Cre+ mice.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Behavior was analyzed using EthoVision software for the number of entries and time spent in open arms.

assays.assay_description: 96 h after psilocybin or saline (48 h after EPM), mice were individually housed 30 min prior and then placed facing a corner of a brightly lit arena (20' x 16', corn cob bedding) containing a food pellet on a white platform; latency to bite was recorded over 5 min (max 300 s), followed by home-cage latency to eat.

application_type.evidence: Psilocybin ... was injected intraperitoneally (i.p.) at a dose of 5 mg/kg

setup_habituation.evidence: Individual housing 30 min prior to testing is described, but no exposure to the test arena before the session

setup_restrain.evidence: Each mouse was placed facing a corner of the arena, and latency to bite at the food pellet was recorded

food_restriction.evidence: a food pellet was placed at the center of the arena ... on a white platform; no food deprivation protocol is described

water_restriction.evidence: No water available in the test arena during the 5-min session

time_to_assay.evidence: then in the novelty suppressed feeding assay 96 h after injection

sample_size.evidence: N = 58 mice (28 males, 30 females; 24 Emx1-Cre-; 34 Emx1-Cre+) were used to assess post-acute anxiety-related behavioral effects of psilocybin.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin reduced latency to feed in the novel arena 96 h post-injection, an effect driven by control females; the anxiolytic effect was abolished in Emx1-Cre+ females and absent in males of both genotypes.
outcomes.statistics: Overall psilocybin: HR = 12.94, z = 2.35, p = 0.019; genotype effect HR = 0.017, z = -2.61, p = 0.009; genotype x drug x sex: HR = 68.57, z = 2.06, p = 0.039; females psilocybin HR = 15.32, 95% CI [1.74, 135.11], z = 2.46, p = 0.014; females drug x genotype HR = 0.014, 95% CI [0.0006, 0.302], z = -2.72, p = 0.0066; males psilocybin HR = 0.65, 95% CI [0.09, 4.60], p = 0.662; males drug x genotype HR = 1.19, 95% CI [0.09, 16.01], p = 0.893
outcomes.evidence: Psilocybin significantly reduced latency to feed suggesting decreased anxiety-like behavior (Fig. 3C and D, HR = 12.94, z = 2.35, p = 0.019). There was a significant effect of genotype on the effect of psilocybin (HR = 0.017, z = -2.61, p = 0.009).

judge_notes: Split the single 30-min open-field session into two assays (Head Twitch Response and Open Field Locomotion) following the rubric rule that the same apparatus used for different behavioural domains counts as separate assays; 2 of 3 candidates did this.
Dropped the whole-brain c-Fos mapping, receptor autoradiography and network/correlation analyses — these are histological/anatomical endpoints, not behavioural assays.
HTR D2 scored 1 (15 min scoring window falls in the 15–60 min inclusive bin), overriding one candidate's '<15 min'.
Open Field Locomotion B2 scored 1: Fig. 2B presents locomotor activity over the 30 min and AUC was computed with trapz, implying a within-session time course.
Open Field Locomotion B1 scored 0: AUC is a derived summary of the same locomotor variable, not a distinct behavioural measure.
EPM and NSF time_to_assay set to short_term_1to7d (48 h and 96 h respectively), overriding candidates that used early_2to24h for 48 h.

NSF food_restriction set to 'no' — a food pellet was accessible in the arena during recording and no fasting protocol is described; 'before' used by two candidates was based on individual housing, which is not food restriction.
NSF E1 kept as Standard apparatus (modal) rather than Enriched arena; the bedding and platform are scored separately under E3/E8.
DOI set to null — the only DOI offered by a candidate was that of the authors' prior Mol Psychiatry paper, not this article.
sex n_male/n_female summed across the acute (10/10), post-acute (28/30) and c-Fos (7/10) cohorts = 45 male / 50 female.
